stories.title: Canton woman gets 16 insurance notices for treatments she never had; provider found billing under her name
stories.summary: A Canton woman received 16 insurance notices for medical treatments she never had, including cancer care. After media intervention, UnitedHealthcare stated a Florida provider billed the claims in her name. The insurer denied the claims, confirming she has no financial responsibility, and explained that benefit statements are issued even for denied claims.

inputFacts.summary: A Canton woman received 16 insurance benefit statements for medical procedures she never underwent, including cancer treatments. stories.title: University of Michigan, Detroit Tigers PA announcer Zach Linfield injured in car crash after MSU game
stories.summary: University of Michigan and Detroit Tigers PA announcer Zach Linfield sustained bruises, chemical burns, and injured fingers in a car crash after a game in Ann Arbor. Canton police and paramedics assisted him at the scene, and he was released from the hospital early Sunday morning.

stories.title: Priced out: Why Ann Arbor housing keeps getting more expensive, and what the city is doing about it
stories.summary: Ann Arbor's housing costs are significantly higher than national averages, with median home prices rising nearly 50% since 2016 to $618,838. The city's Comprehensive Land Use Plan, approved in March 2026, aims to address this by opening up single-family areas to low-rise residential developments, despite some community concerns about gentrification and green spaces.

inputFacts.title: Northville High School to remain open Wednesday with increased police presence after threatening phone call
inputFacts.summary: Northville High School will remain open on Wednesday following a lockdown triggered by a threatening phone call on Tuesday. Police conducted K-9 sweeps and determined the threat was likely a hoax, though an increased police presence will remain at the school as a precaution.

inputFacts.title: Data center restrictions pass in Saginaw Township and Romulus
inputFacts.summary: Saginaw Township and Romulus have both approved new measures to restrict data center development. Saginaw Township passed a detailed ordinance regulating noise, water usage, and location, while Romulus enacted a 180-day moratorium to allow time for drafting permanent regulations.

inputFacts.title: Threatening phone call prompts Northville High School to go into lockdown
inputFacts.summary: Northville High School was placed on lockdown following a threatening phone call on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. Although the school district determined the threat was not credible, law enforcement conducted a building sweep and closed a section of 6 Mile Road as a precaution.

inputFacts.title: New Exhibits
inputFacts.summary: The Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum has introduced two new exhibits: STEAM Park, featuring interactive mechanical installations like a Window Maze and a digital Roulette Curve, and All About You, which explores human anatomy and medical transport through hands-on activities. Both exhibits aim to engage visitors with science and self-discovery.

inputFacts.title: Rob Cantor returns with a ‘bewilderingly great’ new video and album
inputFacts.summary: Musician Rob Cantor is set to release his second solo album, Age of Athleisure, on November 11, 2026. The release is accompanied by a new music video for the track 'Going Purple,' directed by Ben Ketai, which features Cantor's signature blend of electro-pop and absurdist humor.

inputFacts.title: Mother, son charged in human trafficking operation at Oakland County massage businesses
inputFacts.summary: A mother and son have been charged with multiple felonies, including human trafficking and money laundering, following an investigation into massage businesses in Oakland County. Minjie Wu faces additional charges of second-degree criminal sexual conduct.

inputFacts.title: Gardner White kicks off holiday season with Twinkle Town celebration in Novi
inputFacts.summary: Gardner White hosted its fifth annual Twinkle Town celebration at its new Novi Road store, featuring a tree lighting, holiday entertainment, and a visit from Santa Claus. The event included a Parade of Trees where community members can vote for their favorite design through December 8, with the winner receiving $10,000 for a charity of their choice.

inputFacts.title: Woman killed, man injured in double shooting on Detroit’s east side
inputFacts.summary: A woman in her 20s was killed and a man in his 40s was injured during a shooting on the 5800 block of East Outer Drive in Detroit. The incident occurred on November 10, 2026, and remains under investigation by the Detroit Police Department's Homicide Unit.

inputFacts.title: Mother, son accused of human trafficking at Novi massage parlors
inputFacts.summary: Minjie Wu and her son Ruize Wu have been charged with human trafficking, operating a criminal enterprise, and other felonies related to massage parlors in Novi. Investigators allege the pair moved women between businesses and homes, with Minjie Wu also facing a criminal sexual conduct charge following an undercover operation.

inputFacts.title: AAPD Chief Andre C. Anderson announces retirement
inputFacts.summary: Ann Arbor Police Department Chief Andre C. Anderson has announced his retirement. The announcement was reported by The Michigan Daily on November 10, 2026.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor parents press AAPS for stronger school security after string of threats
inputFacts.summary: Parents in Ann Arbor are calling on the Ann Arbor Public Schools district to implement more robust security measures. This push follows a series of recent threats directed at the school system.

inputFacts.title: City gathers feedback on Division Street Bikeway Extension Project during open house
inputFacts.summary: Community members attended an open house at Larcom City Hall to discuss the proposed Division Street Bikeway Extension Project, which aims to improve cyclist and pedestrian safety. The project includes plans to narrow car lanes and convert Carey Street to a one-way road, drawing mixed feedback from residents regarding traffic congestion and environmental impact.

inputFacts.title: Detroit school board candidate raises over $75,500 in 2026 election
inputFacts.summary: Detroit school board candidate Dr. Jameel Smith has raised over $75,500 for the 2026 election, significantly outpacing other candidates in campaign funding. The report details campaign expenditures and contributions for 11 candidates, noting a shift away from traditional advertising spending in this election cycle.
